intro: The cabinet in the back corner of the arcade has been unplugged since 1987. It still has a high-score table, and the initials on it keep changing.

puzzles.title: Warp Zone
puzzles.flavor: The typist in the arcade was consistently, reliably, one step off.
puzzles.hint: Every letter was typed one key to the side on a QWERTY keyboard.

puzzles.title: Up Up Down Down
puzzles.flavor: Every chord is a button. Every button remembers how many times it was hit. Half a turn of the wheel and you'd have it.

partials.b0dd49563f6ce9c612003cdd4db4a640685e9c07: You've decoded it, but it's not finished. One more layer.

puzzles.hint: Each frequency pair is a phone keypad key (DTMF). The ×n is how many times it was pressed: old-school multi-tap texting. Then undo: ROT13.

puzzles.title: Attract Mode
puzzles.flavor: The chemist only ever shopped from the first twenty-six shelves.
puzzles.hint: Each element's atomic number is a letter position (hydrogen = 1 = A).

puzzles.title: Kill Screen
puzzles.flavor: The hands aren't telling the time. They're waving.
puzzles.hint: Each clock's two hands are the two arms of a flag-semaphore signaller (hand length doesn't matter).

puzzles.title: Speedrun
puzzles.flavor: Fences and corners. Some of them have an animal inside.
puzzles.hint: Pigpen (Freemason's) cipher: A–I in a # grid, J–R the same with dots, S–V in an X, W–Z the X with dots.

meta.title: Meta: Insert Coin
meta.flavor: A well-thumbed book of scripture, and a list of verses someone underlined. Its chapters are the reports on this page.
